method: Adjudication pass after reading both raw readings (primary: Codex/GPT-6; blind: claude-opus-5-5) and the comparison file. Every disputed or flagged mark was checked against the enlarged source bands /tmp/morning-s39..s43-band0..3.png (2420px originals, viewed at 2000px; multiply displayed coordinates by 1.21) and the attribution crop /tmp/morning-byline.png (2970px original, viewed at 2000px; multiply by 1.49). No standard siddur or Bible text was used to settle any reading. Block keys and block scopes follow the primary. The one exception is that the standalone word שְׁמָעָה at the bottom of s40 is split out of psalm_38_16 into its own block, psalm_39_13_shimah, because it is the first word of Ps 39:13, which continues at the top of s42. The initial hashes and differences in /tmp/morning-comparison.json stay as the historical record. This output does not claim the two raw readings agreed. Hebrew linkage cues at the start of English paragraphs are left out of the English text. Real Hebrew words inside English rubrics (טלית, ברכה, ציצת) are kept as printed. Meteg is encoded only where I verified it at the two s39 sites asked about; other possible meteg sites are listed under pending_human.

blocks.text: Before draping oneself in the טלית the following is said:

הִנְנִי מִתְעַטֵּף בְּטַלִּית שֶׁל־צִיצִת כְּדֵי לְקַיֵּם מִצְוַת בּוֹרְאִי כַּכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה וְעָשׂוּ לָהֶם צִיצִת עַל־כַּנְפֵי בִגְדֵיהֶם לְדֹרֹתָם. וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁאֲנִי מִתְכַּסֶּה בְטַלִּית בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כֵּן תִּזְכֶּה נִשְׁמָתִי לְהִתְלַבֵּשׁ בְּטַלִּית נָאָה לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא בְּגַן עֵֽדֶן, אָמֵן:
uncertainties: The source quotes only part of Num 15:38 (וְעָשׂוּ לָהֶם צִיצִת עַל־כַּנְפֵי בִגְדֵיהֶם לְדֹרֹתָם), with defective צִיצִת. This is not a full-verse quotation.

blocks.text: Then this ברכה is recited while standing:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ לְהִתְעַטֵּף בַּצִּיצִת:
One then drapes oneself in the טלית and says:
מַה־יָּקָר חַסְדְּךָ אֱלֹהִים וּבְנֵי אָדָם בְּצֵל כְּנָפֶיךָ יֶחֱסָיוּן:
יִרְוְיֻן מִדֶּשֶׁן בֵּיתֶךָ וְנַחַל עֲדָנֶיךָ תַשְׁקֵם:
כִּי עִמְּךָ מְקוֹר חַיִּים, בְּאוֹרְךָ נִרְאֶה־אוֹר:
מְשֹׁךְ חַסְדְּךָ לְיֹדְעֶיךָ וְצִדְקָתְךָ לְיִשְׁרֵי־לֵב:

יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁתְּהֵי חֲשׁוּבָה מִצְוַת צִיצִת זוֹ כְּאִלּוּ קִיַּמְתִּיהָ בְּכָל־פְּרָטֶיהָ וְדִקְדּוּקֶיהָ וְכַוָּנוֹתֶיהָ ותרי״ג מִצְוֹת־הַתְּלוּיִם בָּהּ. אָמֵן:
uncertainties: ותרי״ג is printed unpointed, with gershayim. It is the numeral abbreviation for 613. No expansion and no pointing are added to the text.

blocks.text: One then removes the טלית from the face and drapes oneself in such a way that there should be one ציצת in front and one behind on each side.
Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who has sanctified us with His commandments and ordered us to drape ourselves with show-fringes.

How precious is Thy grace, O God, and the children of man shelter in the shadow of Thy wings. They are refreshed by the felicity of Thy house and with the brook of Thy bliss dost Thou water them. For with Thee is the source of life, in Thy light do we behold light. Extend Thy grace to those who acknowledge Thee, and Thy charity to those who are of upright heart.

וַאֲנִי בְּרֹב חַסְדְּךָ אָבֹא בֵיתֶךָ אֶשְׁתַּחֲוֶה אֶל־הֵיכַל קָדְשְׁךָ בְּיִרְאָתֶךָ:
בְּבֵית אֱלֹהִים נְהַלֵּךְ בְּרָגֶשׁ:

מַה־טֹּבוּ אֹהָלֶיךָ יַעֲקֹב מִשְׁכְּנֹתֶיךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל: וַאֲנִי בְּרֹב חַסְדְּךָ אָבֹא בֵיתֶךָ אֶשְׁתַּחֲוֶה אֶל־הֵיכַל קָדְשְׁךָ בְּיִרְאָתֶךָ: יְיָ אָהַבְתִּי מְעוֹן בֵּיתֶךָ וּמְקוֹם מִשְׁכַּן כְּבוֹדֶךָ: וַאֲנִי אֶשְׁתַּחֲוֶה וְאֶכְרָעָה אֶבְרְכָה לִפְנֵי־יְיָ עֹשִׂי: וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּתִי־לְךָ יְיָ עֵת רָצוֹן אֱלֹהִים בְּרָב־חַסְדֶּךָ עֲנֵנִי בֶּאֱמֶת יִשְׁעֶךָ:

blocks.text: Prayers
On entering the Synagogue:
And I through the abundance of Thy grace enter Thy house and bow down before Thy holy place in awe of Thee.
In the house of God let us walk in throngs.

How becoming are your tents, O Jacob, your dwellings, O Israel. And I through the abundance of Thy grace enter Thy house and bow down before Thy holy place in awe of Thee. O Lord, I love the site of Thy house, the place of the dwelling of Thy glory. I bow, throw myself down and kneel before the Lord, my Maker. And as for me, my prayer is to Thee, O Lord, at a time of favour. O God, in the abundance of Thy grace respond to me with the truth of Thy salvation.

In the morning I seek Thee, my rock and my fortress. I order my morning and also my evening prayer before Thee. Before Thy grandeur I stand and tremble, for Thine eye sees all the thoughts of my heart. What can heart and tongue accomplish, what can my strength, what can the spirit within me. Behold, man’s song pleases Thee. Therefore, I wish to thank Thee as long as God’s breath is in me.
Before the morning prayer:

I call to Thee, for Thou dost respond to me, O God, incline Thine ear to me, hear my word. In righteousness may I behold Thy countenance, I am satisfied on waking with Thy likeness. I trust in Thee, O Lord, I say, Thou art my God. Hear the voice of my prayer when I implore Thee, when I raise my hands toward Thine inmost sanctuary. O Lord my God, I implore Thee and Thou healest me. Unto Thee, O Lord, do I call and my Master do I entreat. Let Thy countenance shine upon Thy servant, help me in Thy grace. For I wait for Thee, O Lord, Thou dost respond, O Lord my God.

blocks.text: Prayers
Hear my prayer, O Lord, listen to my entreaty, at my tears do not be silent.
Hear, O Lord, and be gracious to me, O Lord, be my aid.

Song of the ascents by David: I am glad when they say to me: Let us go into the House of the Lord. I rejoice at Thy word as one who has found abundant booty. Lister to the sound of my cry, my King and my God, for to Thee do I pray. O Lord, in the morning listen to my voice, in the morning I address Thee and I have hope. I called to Thee for Thou dost respond to me. O God, incline Thine ear to me, hear my word. My foot has stood on level ground. In assemblies will I praise the Lord.
The Thirteen Principles
Exalted is the living God and praised. He exists and timeless is His existence.
He is unique and there is nought unique like His uniqueness. He is hidden and infinite too is His unity.
He has not the shape of a body nor is He a body. We cannot estimate His sanctity.
He was there before anything that was created; He is the first and there was no beginning to His beginning.
Behold He is the Master of the world and every creature indicates His grandeur and His rule.
The wealth of His prophecy did He bestow upon men of His possession and His glory.
No other prophet arose in Israel like Moses, who perceived His likeness.
The true Torah has God given to His people through His prophet, the faithful one of His house.
God will not alter nor will He change His law for another unto eternity.
He observes and knows our secrets, perceiving even at its beginning the end of a matter.
He treats man kindly according to his conduct and sends disaster to the wicked according to his wickedness.
He will send our Messiah at the end of days to redeem those who wait for the finality of His salvation.
God will revive the dead in the abundance of His grace. Blessed for ever and ever be His renowned Name.
